name: ai-maestro-visual-communicator-plugin
description: Generate interactive HTML pages — diagrams, diff reviews, plan reviews, slide decks, data tables, and v2 modal-comment agent reports. Every page sends the user's selection (or per-element comment thread) back to the agent.

cpv._intentional_pipeline_drift_rationale: Per canonical-pipeline-migration step 10b (doctor report 20260519_101728+0200-canonical-pipeline-upgrade.md) and step 13 (CHECK-15 ruff UP037 fix): the 8 files listed in `_intentional_pipeline_drift_files` carry INTENTIONAL drift vs the CPV canon. Most are STRICTLY above canon (additional SHA-pins, timeout-minutes, env-sanitization, schema fixes). publish.py is mixed: above on atomic-push + 3-manifest lockstep + dev-browser soft-pass; selective merge of canon's Gates 0/5 + idempotent commit/tag, not full overlay. .markdownlint.json keeps local _comment + MD012 disable. scripts/cpv_network_resilience.py has the string-quoted-annotation removed (UP037: redundant under `from __future__ import annotations`); the canonical CPV version still has the string form. The validator currently emits RC-PIPELINE-DRIFT-001 for each of these as a WARNING (advisory only — does NOT block publish). When CPV implements the `allow_pipeline_drift` allowlist mechanism (referenced in the validator's recommendation text but not yet active in v2.94.0), this list can be promoted to a functional `allow_pipeline_drift` field. See per-step commit messages for the per-file rationale.
cpv._intentional_validator_false_positives_r: Per canonical-pipeline-migration step 12 (doctor report 20260520_063543+0200-post-migration-doctor.md, finding A): four `Possible broken backtick path` WARNINGs against `skills/amvcp-self-debug-rules/SKILL.md` for paths that DO exist on disk. The validator's bare-slug-path heuristic flags backtick-wrapped mentions like `amvcp-iterm2-preview/SKILL.md` that appear in bullet-text without a markdown link wrapper. The same skill file (lines 102-107) correctly links the same 4 skills via `[text](../amvcp-foo/SKILL.md)` form; lines 119-122 use the bare form as descriptive 'See also' labels. The validator should walk the plugin's `skills/<name>/` tree before warning, identical to the resolver used by `Reference to non-existent skill` (the MAJOR-grade resolver) — this is the same class of false-positive as upstream bug #27 but in a different code path. Tracked as candidate upstream bug #30. The affected skill file is on the DO NOT TOUCH list (hand-tuned rule labels per project memory + TRDD-4c300620); the bare-slug form is intentional in those bullet labels. The 4 WARNINGs are advisory only — they do NOT block publish.
